title: I’m turning my homebrew D&D campaign into a 2.5D RPG. Here’s the work-in-progress trailer.
author: OpenToFriends
selftext:
I know there are a lot of games with this 2.5D look going around right now, but this one started with my homebrew D&D campaign, The Central Nexus, which I'm incredibly passionate about. It’s a pretty personal project, and I wanted to share where the game is so far in order to gauge ya'lls thoughts on it. The campaign starts with people arriving in a strange MMO-like world and discovering they can’t log out. Everyone has three lives. There are portals to other worlds, and a 100-floor Tower with the promise that reaching the top lets you decide your fate along with the fate of others within the Central Nexus.

I want you to have a favorite tavern and people you want to check on when you get back from, tons of slice-of-life type events and relationships and friendships, etc. While also enjoying great battles and extreme boss battles. (There will even be a mode where you cannot physically save the game, in order to get you into the mindset of the player, and when you lose all three lives, that's it. Start all over.)

I’m building it in Godot with a lot of help from Claude and Codex...mainly Claude to be honest. I'm using PixelLab for sprites and animation...which hasn't been the best experience and Tripo3D for 3D assets. Keeping everything consistent has been a pain. I’ve had characters equipment change between animation frames, clothing go missing, and oh my god the faces..., so getting a nice-looking character image and getting that character working in the game have been very different problems. A lot of it I've had to physically fix myself.

This trailer is a look at the work in progress. There’s still a massive shit ton to fix and work on...but I'd be lying if I said I haven't loved it every step of the way so far...except for the weekly limits...sigh...but I wanted to start sharing the project while I’m making it.

TLDR: I’m adapting my homebrew D&D campaign into a 2.5D RPG with AI-assisted development. This is the WIP trailer, and I’d appreciate some outside eyes on it.

Thank you for your time and I hope you're having a great day.
